answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and bids for one marble berth in the ocean auction. Every bid enters the echo list, and auditors replay the sort: berths go to the highest bids, each winner pays its bid, and no berth key is reused. Prices rise with demand: the first berth costs 30, so the kth berth costs 30+(k-1). A fake thus pays 70 plus its bid; the thousandth fake pays 1,099, and 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 529,500. A shill-bid ring fails because each winning shill bid must also pay and lock a bond. An honest agent bids once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
